name: Marine Corps Base Hawaii
tagline: On Kaneohe Bay, windward Oahu: home of the 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment and Marine Aircraft Group 24.
_note: Marine Corps base at Kaneohe Bay, windward Oahu (base ZIP 96863). Region flagged OCONUS for the browse UX, but Hawaii is a BAH/RentCast/SchoolDigger state, so it KEEPS the full CONUS template (BAH MHA HI408 = Honolulu County, all of Oahu). Housing: Ohana Military Communities, managed by Hunt (13 neighborhoods incl. Camp Smith and Manana in Pearl City). Schools: Hawaii DOE; Mokapu Elementary is the only school on base (Kailua-Kalaheo complex area). Medical: Branch Health Clinic Kaneohe Bay (no ER); Tripler has the only military ER on Oahu. Corrected 2026-11-15 from Military OneSource (mcb-hawaii), Hunt, HIDOE, MCCS Hawaii and HDOT (page-builder research/mcbh-facts.md). Gate and Visitor Center hours unverified (base pages refuse automated readers). schools_live stays on Kaneohe because a SchoolDigger search for Kailua also returns Kailua-Kona schools. Hawaii is TRICARE West. Medium-confidence flags: base coords (approx), off-base ZIP 96744 (Kaneohe).

data.Major units: 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment; Marine Aircraft Group 24 (MV-22B Ospreys, KC-130Js); 3rd Radio Battalion; the Navy's HSM-37 helicopters
data.Setting: Windward Oahu, between the Koolau mountains and the Pacific
data.Note: Over 25,000 Marines, sailors, family members and civilian employees live and work here (Military OneSource)

sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Marine Corps Base Hawaii sits at Kaneohe Bay on the windward side of Oahu. Over 25,000 Marines, sailors, family members and civilian employees live and work there, and Military OneSource gives its mission as providing facilities and services that support combat readiness. It hosts the 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, Marine Aircraft Group 24 with MV-22B Osprey and KC-130J squadrons at Marine Corps Air Station Kaneohe Bay, 3rd Radio Battalion and the Navy's HSM-37 helicopter squadron.

The setting is spectacular, framed by the Koolau mountains and the ocean, but it is still an island posting: Oahu homes are often small, only one car ships at government cost, and the side of the mountains you live on shapes your commute, your school complex area and your flood and tsunami checks.

data.subtitle: Three highways cross the Koolau mountains between the base and the rest of Oahu: H-3, Likelike and Pali. The side you live on sets your commute and shapes your schools and your flood and tsunami checks.
intro: The base is on the windward side of the Koolau mountains. Hawaii DOT sends drivers from one crossing to the others during work, Tropical Storm Lala closed the Pali Highway both ways on August 16, 2026, and an H-3 on-ramp in Kaneohe has been closed for emergency culvert repairs.
So where a spouse works matters too. Schools are assigned by address within complex areas: base housing at Kaneohe Bay and Kailua are in the Kailua-Kalaheo complex area, Kaneohe in Castle-Kahuku.

recommendations.advice: Ohana Military Communities (Hunt) runs 13 neighborhoods, with no damage deposit and what Hunt calls "Average Utilities Included" (features vary). Mokapu Elementary is on base. Contact the Family Housing Department (808-496-2676) as soon as you have orders.

About 10 minutes to the Mokapu Gate and 14 to the H-3 main gate (no-traffic estimates), in the same Kailua-Kalaheo school complex area as base housing at Kaneohe Bay. Zillow's typical home value is $1,526,023 and typical rent $3,753 (September 2026).

About 13 minutes to the H-3 main gate (no-traffic estimate), in the Castle-Kahuku complex area. Typical home value $1,081,692 and rent $3,645 (Zillow, September 2026). Heavy rain flooded homes here on February 21, 2026, so check the flood zone.

Manana in Pearl City is part of the Marine housing system and open to active-duty Army, Navy, Air Force and Marines: an option for a dual-military family with one member at Pearl Harbor, or a spouse who works there. Aiea and Pearl City are about 25 to 29 minutes from the H-3 main gate (no-traffic estimates).

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Military OneSource says to enter through the main gate on the H-3 freeway; the Mokapu Gate is the back gate on the Kailua side.
Visitors need a sponsor. The Pass House (Visitor Center) is in Building 1637 at the main gate, 808-257-2047 (MyBaseGuide, 2021); call ahead for hours.
We couldn't confirm gate hours from an official page, so check them with the base before you go.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: Ohana Military Communities, managed by Hunt Military Communities, runs base housing for Marine families at Kaneohe Bay and Camp H. M. Smith. Hunt lists 13 neighborhoods, including Camp Smith, where Marine Forces Pacific is based (E-9, O-4 and O-5 only), and Manana in Pearl City (144 single homes for staff NCO and officer families and 24 duplex homes for junior enlisted families, open to active-duty Army, Navy, Air Force and Marines).
Hunt lists no application fees, no damage deposit, no first and last month's rent and what it calls "Average Utilities Included" (features vary by floor plan and neighborhood). Leasing: 808-657-3386.
The Family Housing Department is at 1571 Lawrence Rd. (808-496-2676). Register there before you negotiate any off-base lease, or you can lose Temporary Lodging Allowance (Military OneSource).

source.label: DoD 2026 BAH Rates, MHA HI408 (Honolulu County)

sections.title: Schools
data: There are no DoD schools in Hawaii; children attend the Hawaii State Department of Education's public schools, assigned by home address. Mokapu Elementary is the only school on the base: pre-kindergarten to grade 6, more than 780 students; the first phase of its rebuilt campus opened in January 2026.

Mokapu is in the Kailua-Kalaheo complex area. The state's list of windward schools with many military children names Mokapu, Aikahi Elementary, Kailua Intermediate, Kainalu Elementary and Kalaheo High; Kaneohe schools are in the Castle-Kahuku complex area. This list isn't a zoning map, so check the schools for your address. School Liaison: 808-496-2019 (Military OneSource and the state list it; MCCS Hawaii's page also shows 808-257-2019).

data.Clinic: Branch Health Clinic Kaneohe Bay, Bldg. 6905, Harris Ave.: 808-496-3365, weekdays 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.
data.Care: Medical and dental clinics on base, no emergency room; clinic patients are often referred to Tripler Army Medical Center, which has the only military ER on Oahu (Military OneSource)

source.label: Military OneSource, MCB Hawaii health care

data.Exchange: Marine Corps Exchange, Mokapu Mall, Building 6109: 808-496-4832

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves. On Oahu, price the property tax before you buy a home you might rent out later: with no home exemption, a home assessed at $1 million or more pays the Residential A rate, $11.40 per $1,000 above the first $1 million (fiscal 2027).
rent: Your tour is a standard length and you'll PCS off the island.
Home prices on Oahu are out of comfortable reach for your budget.
On-base housing covers you without overextending.
You want flexibility in an expensive, competitive market.
buy: You expect a long tour or plan to keep a home in Hawaii long term.
You can afford Oahu's high entry price and want to build equity.
You're comfortable being a long-distance landlord after you PCS.
You've found a property and location you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Zillow's typical home value is $1,526,023 in Kailua and $1,081,692 in Kaneohe (September 2026), so buying makes sense mainly for long or repeat tours and bigger budgets. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, and talk to a lender and an agent who know the island and military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics, and a Hawaii PCS adds island-specific steps like shipping a vehicle. Start early.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Allowance (TLA) for OCONUS/Hawaii while you house-hunt; know the rules before you travel.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your command and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Contact the Family Housing Department (808-496-2676) as soon as you have orders, and register there before you negotiate any off-base lease; Military OneSource says skipping it can cost you Temporary Lodging Allowance.

steps.title: Sort your vehicle and access
steps.text: Only one car ships at government cost; the Navy's Opportune Lift can carry a second from San Diego, but that can take up to a year. When your car arrives, take it for a Hawaii safety inspection (it fails at first only for lacking Honolulu registration), get an out-of-state permit or register in Honolulu, then go back within 30 days of that first check to pass. Learn the visitor-pass process for guests.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Call the School Liaison (808-496-2019). Hawaii assigns schools by address, so you can't enroll until you have one; bring records and immunizations, and a physical for students new to Hawaii.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE enrollment for the Kaneohe Bay clinic. There's no ER on base; Tripler Army Medical Center has the only military ER on Oahu.

data.q: Is MCB Hawaii a real overseas tour?
data.a: It's in Hawaii, a U.S. state, so it uses stateside pay tools like BAH (not OHA). But it's a true island posting with shipping, high costs, and accompanied-tour planning, which is why we flag it under the OCONUS/island group.

No official source says how many live on base. Base housing (Ohana Military Communities, Hunt) has 13 neighborhoods, including Manana in Pearl City; off base, Kailua and Kaneohe are about 10 to 13 minutes from a gate and Aiea and Pearl City about 25 to 29 (no-traffic estimates).

Zillow's typical home value is $1,526,023 in Kailua and $1,081,692 in Kaneohe, and typical rent $3,753 and $3,645 (September 2026; rents include apartments). An E-5 with dependents receives $3,663 a month in BAH in 2026.
MCB Hawaii is MHA HI408, which covers all of Oahu (Honolulu County). Because it's a U.S. state, you get BAH; use the calculator above for your grade.

data.q: Is there an ER on base?
data.a: No. The Branch Health Clinic Kaneohe Bay is open weekdays, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., and Tripler Army Medical Center has the only military emergency room on Oahu. A civilian hospital may be closer to your home, so find your nearest ER before you need it. In an emergency, call 911.
Only one car ships at government cost per PCS order to Hawaii. The Navy's Opportune Lift program can carry a second vehicle from San Diego, but that can take up to a year.
